column10: Where plates push together the land is young and rugged.
Where plates pull apart the land breaks into scarps and rift valleys.
A mountain range is rugged throughout and drains too fast to be marshy.
A subrange's crest is cliffs and peaks.
A massif is a knot of cliffs and peaks.
A peak is bare rock above the tree line.
A pass is a saddle: rugged but not a summit.
A desert has little standing water and few trees.
An erg is a sea of dunes.
A salt flat is a dead-level crust of salt.
An oasis is a wet hollow where ground water comes near the surface.
A large river's banks are a wet valley floor
